archetypes.name: auth-surface
archetypes.rationale: Targets whether the plan fully closes the env-key auth gap across every scoped Codex exec surface without leaving bypasses.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the plan's claimed six Codex exec surfaces against the scoped files and repository evidence. Look for missed direct invocations, inconsistent auth-helper usage, or places where the proposed launcher or inline wiring would not actually preserve OPENAI_API_KEY preference. Check whether any planned suppressions or linter scope exclusions could allow the original defect to recur. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: launcher-contracts
archetypes.rationale: Focuses on contract drift between the new shared launcher, existing run-external-agent semantics, sidecars, retries, and collectors.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the proposed launch-codex-exec.sh contract matches the existing run-external-agent, collect-agent-results, timing, usage, and sidecar conventions it intends to preserve. Hunt for plan gaps around argv shape, stdin behavior, CODEX_HOME lifetime, auth retry handling, output files, and background collection. Verify that negotiation being wired inline is contractually compatible with its documented exit grammar and event stream. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-coverage
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether the test and lint plan would prove the proposed auth sweep and prevent regressions rather than only checking happy paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Evaluate the planned harnesses, Makefile targets, pre-commit hook, and linter rules against the actual changes they are meant to validate. Look for untested edge cases, brittle fixture assumptions, missing shard coverage, false positives or false negatives in the static guard, and assertions that would not catch a broken auth implementation. Compare proposed test updates with existing harness style and documented lint conventions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
